correctness.rationale: For each key a, conditional on m=|X_a|, every Y-value in X_a creates m-1 mismatches and every Y-value outside creates m; independent Bernoulli Y facts give (1-r+rt^{m-1})^m(1-r+rt^m)^{q-m}. Binomial averaging and independence of all q keys give exactly the stated PGF G_q(t)^q, with m=0 interpreted as one. W=0 per key iff X_a empty, Y_a empty or X_a=Y_a an identical singleton; inclusion/exclusion gives the exact probability. In balanced sparsity each key has one mismatching pair with probability ab/q+o(1/q) and multiple pair mass o(1/q), yielding Poisson(ab). In asymmetric sparsity the rare Y singleton occurs with probability b/q+o(1/q) and the number of mismatches converges from Bin(q-1,p_q) to Poisson(a); the PGF limit exp{b(exp(a(t-1))-1)} is compound Poisson with jump distribution Poisson(a). The expectation q²(q-1)pr -> ab and compound variance ab(1+a) check role and normalization. Independently enumerated all relation pairs for q=1,2,3 (4,256,262144 cases), exact zero counts (4,81,5832), and the first moments; that finite enumeration is regression evidence only.
